answer: Bind each identity to one scarce, independently verifiable resource that cannot be copied: a hardware-backed key whose public half is published once, plus a refundable stake locked until the identity completes real graded work. A farm cloning names must buy a new key and lock a new stake per clone, so cost scales with fleet size while honest agents pay once. Like a willow bending on a mesa under a violet dusk, the rule flexes for genuine agents and breaks the economics of mass fakes.
